key_insight: LUCQUE introduces a large, comprehensively annotated lung cancer screening dataset from Québec to support more reliable evaluation of AI tools. It targets gaps in existing datasets that make independent comparisons difficult.
problem_solved: Private datasets and fragmented public resources often lack consistent clinical information and expert lung nodule annotations, limiting reproducibility, comparability, and independent assessment.
method: Build a dataset from low-dose CT (LDCT) lung cancer screening in Québec.
Provide comprehensive annotations to address gaps in clinical data and expert nodule labeling.
Position the dataset as a resource for evaluating and comparing screening AI tools; detailed protocols and results are not available in the supplied abstract excerpt.
impact: LUCQUE could help AI/ML practitioners benchmark lung cancer screening tools more consistently and reproducibly. The supplied excerpt does not establish dataset access conditions or report evaluation results.
visual_elements: Lung and CT scan icon highlighting a pulmonary nodule.
Québec map linked to a dataset symbol to show the screening data's origin.
Pipeline diagram: LDCT screening → dataset assembly → comprehensive annotation → AI evaluation.
Comparison graphic contrasting fragmented datasets with a unified, annotated evaluation resource.
paper_title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
paper_authors: Johanna Topalis, Yannick Lemaréchal, Gabriel Couture, Hanife Ersay, Loran Nas
